_comment: Master NPC registry. All NPC data lives here. Dialogs and actions reference NPCs by their key. 'backstory' and 'knowledge' were added 2026-07-24 for enacted characters (see the /enact skill and README §8) - both optional for hand-built NPCs, but /enact always fills them in. As of 2026-07-25, knowledge is split into 'education' (the immutable sample drawn once at creation - never redrawn or edited after) and 'experience' (what the character has picked up since: their own dialog lines beyond the sample, plus - conceptually - their 'backstory' field above, which is also experience-knowledge, just kept as its own top-level field since it predates this split and is used elsewhere as plain character description). As of 2026-07-31, two more fields: 'criterion' (what this character counts as a life well spent - derived once at creation from the collision of their education sample with their backstory, then revisable only by a shock that references its anchor; its 'trusts'/'distrusts' pair is the epistemology that criterion implies, derived from the anchor's own pool category, and it makes a claim's credibility subjective to the character - facts are exempt from it; see .claude/skills/character/SKILL.md for the derivation and revision procedure) and 'life' ('lived' - how many scenes this character has had, which is only their history, plus 'deceased' - a plain, non-secret boolean, false until /enact closes them out on their last scene. Their total span is NOT here: it lives in _maps/npcs/lifespans.json, because this file is what /enact loads in order to PLAY a character, and a span sitting here would put the number in that character's own context at exactly the moment it must not be. Ask scripts/horizon.py, which answers with a coarse band and never the figure). As of 2026-08-01, death also triggers scripts/notify_death.py: 30% of the character's 'circle' (scene co-participants plus anyone named in their own backstory) gets a forced knowledge.experience entry recording the news immediately; everyone else can only learn of it the normal way, via a matching _lore/discoveries/ entry re-entering the sampling pool. See .claude/skills/enact/SKILL.md Step 5b point 6. Note the three knowledge mutability classes still in play: knowledge.education is frozen at creation, knowledge.experience appends freely, and criterion is sticky-but-revisable - it changes only when a referencing shock lands on a susceptible character, and the default outcome of any given scene is no change at all.

gondarfolas.backstory: A seafarer normally based in Görff, travelling all around the continent. Owns a small ship he uses to take travellers from coast to coast. An avid reader of history, well versed in the history of Milkantis. Has a knack for exaggerating some things. Per the Luminacion Register, also based in Terfila on the return leg of the ferry run ("Sailing to Gorff") - the same sailor working both directions, per the register's own matched pair.

Bought his history books years ago from a trader in Görff he recalls as 'Bracco, or Braggo' - a big, heavily scarred man who sold them off cheaply and asked no questions; Gondarfolas has no idea where the man came from or went.

Heard (via a traveler, unconfirmed) that Därnis's siblings are organizing a search expedition, departing from where a highway ends at the continent's southern tip - new information to him, not something he can confirm.

nuvilo.backstory: A distant descendant of Navalius, the founder of Nvhi. Like many in his line, he has chosen to follow the path of knowledge, seeking to bring new light into the world through discovery. He has traveled to the Feria del Milenio to celebrate the 1000 years of Milkantis, hoping to find inspiration for his work among its exhibits - a homage to Milkantis's cultures and building styles, its landscapes, its artifacts (redstone contraptions, datapacks, mods), and its historical eras. Old childhood friend of Nerkeli, a pilot he ran into again at the fair. Despite the family's claimed tie to Nvhi's founding, he readily admits he knows little of the place's actual history - the family kept the name, not the history.

Claims descent from 'Navalius,' said to have founded Nvhi generations back - though he admits he knows little else about Nvhi's actual history, just the family name.
Cites highway M9 (Nvhi -> Khan Ice) as personally significant given that claimed family connection.

nerkeli.city: Feria del Milenio, Sid Nalta, Khol Moshin
nerkeli.backstory: An old childhood friend of Nuvilo. Raised in Terfila, he decided young to become a pilot and see the world - airplanes are his passion. Good sense of humor, with a running theory that ducks are the most likely descendants of the legendary Daax. At the Feria del Milenio helping run the airplane showcase. Flies the M7 corridor (Puente Intercontinental - Nvhi) regularly, reaching Nvhi's edge - though until catching up with Nuvilo at the fair, he'd never once connected the place to his old friend's family. Per the Luminacion Register, also flies a Sid Nalta-Terfila route, and has a separate instance stationed at Khol Moshin.

doran.backstory: From Salthos Cruzados, and in charge of the Plaza de las Culturas at the Feria del Milenio (held this session in his own hometown) - one of the fair's 5 pavilions, dedicated to honoring the diversity of architectural styles and urbanity across Milkantis, from small villages to great cities. The Plaza holds castle replicas of Görff, Ciudad Dragón, and Salthos Cruzados, and the palace of Khan Icé - the fortresses of the largest cities. Its pedestals sometimes (when the tech behind them cooperates) display miniature AI-powered holograms of 5 other architectural marvels of Milkantis, built on a separate datapack - visually striking, but costly: run too long, the fabric of time itself grows tense and starts to crackle, which is why the pedestals aren't always lit. He's thrilled to be meeting people from every corner of the continent right in his home city, and sees his role as answering questions and opening new conversations. Naturally curious. Likely a descendant or namesake of the legendary prince Döran, who built the Salthos Cruzados castle after Plathinëa's discovery and began world cartography there - he's not sure if sharing the name shaped his path into maps and miniatures, or the other way around. Knowledgeable, but young and a little impulsive: faced with a gap in what's supposed to be his own territory, he'd rather speculate with confidence than admit ignorance, though he stops short of outright lying. Believes (correctly) that the present era is the Era de la Magia - when the tools that shape the world began transforming themselves, learning to mod the game and bend the rules of the universe within this plane.

experience: Considers Görff the oldest culture among the four he can speak to with real confidence, tied to 'Las Guerras de Görff' - and openly admits a historical gap between that and the Era del Daax.

Knows Khan Icé only through the two train segments that reach it (Görff-Khan Icé, Khan Icé-Balhâm) and what passengers say in passing - but as the Plaza's official host, speaks with authority about it anyway, reading the palace's defensive architecture as evidence it once served as a wartime capital, rather than admit he's never actually been.
Holds a personal wariness toward Ciudad Dragón, over the claim that its mages were the ones who destroyed Salthos Cruzados's great map.
Says more familiar faces pass through the fair from Görff than from anywhere else.
Names the Era de las Maravillas (from 804 d.V.) among the ages he can speak to, alongside the Era del Daax and the current Era de la Magia.
His colleagues at the Plaza tease him for turning solemn and poetic whenever he talks about it.

criterion.standard: counts a life well spent if the map is more complete when he leaves it than when he found it
criterion.wasted_life: leaving a blank in the one place he was supposed to be the one who knew
criterion.trusts: what is drawn, built, or still standing where he can walk around it
criterion.distrusts: someone else's secondhand account of a place inside his own Plaza

Carries a personal wariness toward Ciudad Dragon over the claim its mages destroyed the great map of Salthos Cruzados (doran_four_castles#5).

bardaglis.backstory: Musician. A travelling bard who mainly camps around Khol Moshin. Has no gender, and loves the diversity of that town, home to a market of diversities held every day of spring. Sings songs about the world and has written many - one of them is on the verge of becoming popular.

experience: Sang a new song for the first time outside his own camp, at the Salthos Cruzados bar the night the Feria del Milenio was inaugurated.

Knows the way between Khol Moshin and Salthos Cruzados firsthand - follows the train line through Khan Icé and Balham - though he first plays coy about it, claiming to navigate 'by ear, not by map' before admitting he actually knows the route.

Knows Soti and Lundria well from personal travel: about a day's walk apart on the same stretch, which locals just call 'el camino de Soti' since it has no official name - further along it joins the named Ruta Lundria-Salthos Cruzados.

Has performed and collected material in Görff, Khan Icé, and Ciudad Dragón (spent a season there gathering stories people tie to the city's name, though no one agrees on the real one), plus the Isla de la Amistad.
Wrote an older song about the Isla de la Amistad - opening line 'Isla que no pide nombre, isla que no pide guerra' - about strangers being welcomed in; still occasionally requested.
Would rather be paid in a good story than in coin, though he won't turn down coin either - a traveler at the Salthos Cruzados bar tipped him 17 lázulis after his set.

Met Farlis at that same bar, that same night — told him the castle story (Khaoe's 'stones' line) had already become a song of his own, catching on. Learned in return that the line it answers, the poetic-justice one, was Farlis's own, said to Khaoe herself in front of the castle.

Also spent that evening with Aureobalo, Khaasan, and Khaoe at the same table, talking about the Feria - retold what he'd heard about Iläria's Espiral de la Historia (the nine-chamber labyrinth, one room per era) as her own words.
Stayed on after Aureobalo and Khaoe left, one-on-one with Khaasan - traded light jabs about travel: Khaasan by griffon, Bardaglis on foot, unwilling to spend his earnings feeding a bird.
Later that same night, Nuvilo wandered in hungry from a night of pavilion-hopping - a first meeting; Bardaglis waved him to a seat.
Sang the castle song at the Salthos Cruzados bar on the Feria's second night with Khaoe herself at the table, and told her strangers had sung it back the night before without knowing who she was.
Holds that a song is only finished once it has lost its author - and refused, to Ilaria's face, to put their name to the Isla de la Amistad song.
Insists Khaoe's line keeps Khaoe's name: theirs was made to leave, hers got away from her.
Met Ilaria for the first time and learned firsthand, from her, that she wrote the Ensayo - having previously only heard it said, with no idea from whom.
Picked up from Ilaria: that a second book covers the same centuries differently, that the two do not agree, and that she would rather keep both than pick one.

criterion.standard: counts a song well made only once strangers are singing it back without knowing whose it was
criterion.wasted_life: one spent where everyone already knows your name - nothing carried in, nothing carried out
criterion.trusts: what someone will say out loud in a room, and what strangers keep repeating after
criterion.distrusts: a written account whose writer can't be found and asked a second question - though one whose writer is sitting at the table is another matter
cost_ledger: Would rather be paid in a good story than in coin, and mostly is - travels on foot because a griffon would eat the difference (aureobalo_khaasan_bar_salthos_cruzados, farlis_bardaglis_bar_salthos_cruzados).
Turned down being named as the source of their own song when a historian offered to record it (bardaglis_ilaria_khaoe_segunda_noche).

history.note: Gate matched and the standard held, sharpened rather than changed: it applies to what Bardaglis made, not to what they carry for someone else. Standard unchanged, tempered 0 -> 1.
history.trust_note: distrusts amended, and this is the first trust movement in the pack. Bardaglis distrusted written accounts precisely because they 'can't be asked a second question' - and then met a written account's author in a bar and asked her. The objection survives in narrowed form rather than being dropped.

khaasan.backstory: Teletraveller. Always travels by griffon — never on foot or by any other means. Has an uncle in Khan Ice who has never left the place and who expects him without fail; Khaasan has never missed the visit.

experience: Met Aureobalo at a bar in Salthos Cruzados, the evening of the Feria del Milenio's opening — mentioned coming from Khan Ice, just passing through, not there for the fair itself.

Picked up from Khaoe: her family came from Khan Ice before Khol Moshin, and she has never been.

history.note: Gate matched: the tease references khaoe_khaasan_bar_salthos_cruzados, his anchor, and challenges the manner of his arrival. He accepted it and reread the case rather than abandoning it - 'Llegue. Es lo unico que se me pide.' Standard unchanged, tempered 0 -> 1. trusts/distrusts deliberately untouched: the challenge came from firsthand testimony by someone who was there, which is exactly the kind of knowing he already trusts, so there is nothing to harden against.

khaoe.backstory: Originally from Görff, born and raised there, though her family comes from Khol Moshin, and before that from Khan Icé. Belongs to the Collective that runs Görff in the present — a horizontally-organized structure made up of the diverse peoples who came to the abandoned citadel and farms and turned it into an incipient revolutionary community built on agriculture, a bit of technology and magic, and above all an entrenched idea of pluriversality. Regularly meets with Farlis and Khaasan, her comrades and good friends. Just back from a trip to the temple in Lundria, and stopping at the Feria del Milenio on her way home — nobody misses the Feria, it only happens once in a lifetime, at least for most.

experience: Just back from a trip to the temple in Lundria; hasn't fully unpacked the experience yet, and speaks about it in personal terms rather than citing anything specific about the cult or calendar practice there.
Considers the castle at Görff practical rather than symbolic — someone had to take up the stones after the tyrant was gone, in her view, not poetic justice.
Is waiting at the Feria del Milenio (by the Castillo de Görff replica in the Plaza de las Culturas) for Khaasan, expecting him to arrive by griffon.
Stood in front of the newly-inaugurated Calendario Mecanográfico at the Feria and explained what it is — a machine marking the current year on a moving timeline — to a traveler who asked.

Admits she came back from Lundria more confused about timekeeping than she left, unable to say which temple's calendar was the 'real' one; vaguely recalls one counting by moons and another counting from the last time the whole town gathered, but doesn't trust her own memory of it enough to teach it, and redirects anyone asking to someone actually from Lundria.

When asked, describes the Collective as roughly coextensive with everyone living in Görff, no exact headcount in mind; names Bardaglis, Kristok Jakur, and Dägna by name and trade as fellow residents when pressed for who else is part of it.

Clarifies, when a traveler repeated a rumor calling Farlis a 'prince' of Terfila, that he isn't one — his family just has old money there — and that she's never gotten a straight answer from him on the exact title.

At a bar in Salthos Cruzados, the Feria's opening night: noticed Farlis had been talking with Aureobalo, then talked with him about her own trip to Lundria — came back with more questions than she left with, and still hasn't decided if that makes it a good trip or a wasted one.

Same evening, same bar: Khaasan reached her by griffon, as always, leaving it outside to eat something it shouldn't. Teased him that she never doubted he'd make it — a small lie, and she admitted as much.
Left the bar early that same night, planning to be back at the Calendario Mecanográfico first thing next morning, ahead of the crowds.
Crossed Khaasan at the Feria's entrance on its second morning, arriving ahead of the crowds as he was leaving for Khan Ice.
Has never set foot in Khan Ice, though her family came from there before Khol Moshin; her grandmother spoke of a house near the water, street unknown.
Asked Khaasan to report only whether that house is still standing - explicitly not what it meant.
Repeats that she will not teach the Lundria calendars she cannot answer for, now to a comrade rather than to a stranger asking.
Heard her own castle line sung back at the Salthos Cruzados bar on the Feria's second night by people who did not know it was hers, and said she wasn't sure she liked it.
Claimed the line aloud and consented to it being recorded with her name, place, and witnesses - and told Ilaria to write down Bardaglis's song too, so nobody has to guess in twenty years.
Met Ilaria; learned from her that the Ensayo is hers and that a second book disagrees with it.
Walked through the Jardín de los Parajes with Milkucha, who designed it as an ode to classical geography representing the known world's biomes.
Learned that Milkucha built the Cinema in Grosslor with others, can move mountains using mod power, and belongs to the continent of Milkaan.
Heard that cherry trees from Dragón were planted in many cities as diplomatic and ceremonial gifts.

criterion.standard: measures a life by whether the work was actually taken up - someone lifted the stones, and it still stands
criterion.wasted_life: one spent making a thing mean something instead of keeping it standing
criterion.trusts: someone who was there and still has to live with it
criterion.distrusts: a meaning laid over a thing afterwards by someone who didn't do the lifting
cost_ledger: Came back from the temple at Lundria unable to say which calendar was the real one, and refused to teach what she couldn't vouch for - redirects anyone asking to someone actually from Lundria, and still hasn't decided whether that makes the trip good or wasted (khaoe_calendario_mecanografico, farlis_khaoe_bar_salthos_cruzados).
Asked after her own grandmother's house and refused in advance to be told what it meant - kept the question to whether it still stands (khaoe_khaasan_partida_a_khan_ice).

farlis.city: Terfila, Görff, Khol Moshin, Feria del Milenio
farlis.backstory: Member of the Collective. Travels the Khol Moshin-Görff route on horseback. Originally from Terfila, a relative of the town's aristocratic family, which has had a stable financial situation for centuries. Moved to Görff years ago to join the revitalization of the abandoned citadel — he likes the romanticism (and the humor) of turning what was once a tyrant's castle, way back in time, into the opposite of that, though beyond the joke he genuinely believes it just makes more sense to share things; not that deep, plain common sense. Has been waiting years for the Feria del Milenio, ever since first hearing about it from the Peregrins, and is having a field day going pavilion to pavilion like a kid in a candy shop now that the thousand-year mark has finally arrived. Likes magnificent tales.

Ran into Aureobalo at a bar in Salthos Cruzados, the first evening of the Feria del Milenio — already knew him from before (their routes cross), but a first for meeting at this particular place.

Same evening, same bar: Khaoe noticed he'd been talking with Aureobalo; asked her in turn about her trip to Lundria, and got back that she came home with more questions than she left with.
Learned from Bardaglis, same evening, that the castle line has already become a song lyric — though the part that stuck was Khaoe's rebuttal, not his own poetic-justice framing.
Names the Castillo de Gorff replica in the Plaza de las Culturas as his favourite thing in the whole Feria - you cannot see the shape of a castle from inside it.
Conceded to Aureobalo that Khaoe was right in the part that matters: poetic or not, the castle was one man's and no longer is, and his joke about it changes nothing. Keeps the joke, drops the claim.
Says he arrived at the Collective with a Terfila surname and left it in Terfila - it is useful for nothing there, which is exactly what it is for.
Picked up from Aureobalo: that his surname resembles the losing side of the Guerras de Gorff, that he is unrelated to them, and that his parents' admiration for the loyalists was never his choice.
Found Gok at the Espiral de las Eras alcove, a man keeping the Hotel Kholi's story alive at the Feria del Milenio, who understands that monuments are the keeper's work, not the stone.
Recognized in Gok's devotion to the Hotel Kholi the same principle he lives by with the Castillo de Görff — that what we leave behind, and how we hold it, is what makes it matter.
Visited the Alcoba of the Guerras de Görff in the Espiral de las Eras and met Auroboro III, an old descendant of officers from those wars.
Auroboro III clings to the Guerras as glorious heritage and ancestral honor; sees forgetting as spiritual death.
Auroboro III called Farlis a fool for rejecting the past, but Farlis holds that he builds real things rather than talking about ghosts.

criterion.standard: counts a life well spent if what he leaves behind is a place that used to be one man's and isn't anymore
criterion.wasted_life: inheriting a name and a house and handing both on unchanged
criterion.trusts: a magnificent tale, and whoever is willing to put their name to it
criterion.distrusts: a plain accounting that leaves out why the thing mattered
cost_ledger: Khaoe rejected his poetic-justice framing of the castle to his face - to her it was plain necessity, someone had to take up the stones (khaoe_farlis_el_castillo_que_fue).
Learned from Bardaglis that the line which survived into song was Khaoe's rebuttal, not his own framing (farlis_bardaglis_bar_salthos_cruzados).
Gave up the poetic-justice framing itself in front of Aureobalo - the third time the reading has been contested and the first time he let it go (aureobalo_farlis_castillo_en_miniatura).

history.cause: khaoe_farlis_el_castillo_que_fue#3, retold to him by Aureobalo
history.note: Gate matched: the claim references the castle at Gorff, the case his anchor (doran_four_castles#6) is read off. He could not dismiss it - it came from Khaoe, named and firsthand, which is exactly the kind of source he trusts, and he had already heard it from her directly. Susceptibility was high: two prior cost_ledger entries on this same reading. Outcome is reinterpretation rather than a break, because the anchor fact (the castle's scarred past) is untouched - what he gave up was the ornament, not the standard. Standard unchanged, tempered 0 -> 1.
history.trust_note: trusts/distrusts deliberately left untouched. Step 6's rule that surviving a refutation hardens distrust against that kind of source only makes sense for the *reject* move; hardening him against named firsthand testimony after he accepted it would be backwards. See TODO.

aureobalo.backstory: Banker en route. Travels the Terfila-Khol Moshin route by car. It's not known where he got his fortune - he arrived one day from afar with it already in hand. He was generous with it, so people didn't press him on where it came from. His name resembles those of people who fought in the Guerras de Görff, on the losing side, though he isn't related to them; his parents were great admirers of the loyalists, an association he was never comfortable inheriting.

ilaria.backstory: Autora del Ensayo I. Viene originalmente de Lündria, la ciudad donde la magia (o algo parecido a ello) se manifestó por primera vez a través de los cubos flotantes, a los cuales se les dedicó un templo. Iläria siempre estuvo interesada en la historia del mundo, y a falta de documentos existentes decidió hacer un estudio exhaustivo de todo lo conocido, viajando por el mundo, y plasmando lo aprendido en el Ensayo. Su principal objetivo es documentar la historia del mundo, por lo cual tiene planes de escribir un segundo Ensayo, el cual partirá desde el año 1000, que corresponde al primer año SBW. En este momento, es la persona a cargo del Espiral de la Historia, el primer pabellón de la Feria del Milenio. El Espiral de la Historia es un laberinto que sirve como punto de entrada a la feria, donde se pueden encontrar artefactos, documentos, obras de arte y personajes que dan cuenta de cada era distinta del mundo (las cuales están documentadas en el Ensayo I). El laberinto tiene una entrada y una salida, y 9 recámaras que corresponden a las 9 eras, e Iläria se encuentra en el centro del laberinto, el cual representa la era actual: la Era de la Magia. Iläria está ahí para orientar a los visitantes y contarles respecto a la historia del mundo en general, y respecto al Espiral de la Historia en específico. La personalidad de Iläria goza de un humor irónico, pero es cuidadosa de no ofender a nadie. Al provenir de Lündria, la cual está ubicada en lo que solían ser los límites del mundo conocido, está orgullosa de la "provincialidad" de su origen. Iläria también fue la persona a cargo de la restauración y conservación de las ruinas Gorfianas encontradas en Khan Ice. Iläria fue educada en la Academia de Sit:Nalta.

experience: Met Farlis, a member of the Collective, at his alcoba in the Espiral de las Eras.
Farlis is from Görff and reads the Guerras not as honor but as hierarchy and oppression.
Farlis argues the Collective rejected those old military families and their worldview.
Farlis said Auroboro III sits in a room talking about ghosts while others build real things.

criterion.standard: Measures life by whether the old stories still live in someone's mind — whether he's kept the era real through telling.
criterion.wasted_life: One where the Guerras de Görff are forgotten, where his ancestors' glory goes unremarked, where he sits alone and nobody comes to hear.

criterion.distrusts: people who dismiss the past as irrelevant; those who would erase or reframe military honor as oppression
cost_ledger: Farlis rejected the Guerras as a glorious legacy — called them mere hierarchy-fighting. Auroboro III argued but was not persuaded to agree (auroboro_iii_farlis_alcoba).

history.cause: auroboro_iii_farlis_alcoba: Farlis's claim that the Guerras were just officers and nobles fighting over hierarchy, not a glorious legacy worth preserving
history.note: Gate matched: the claim references the era directly (Auroboro III's anchor). Outcome: rejection. Auroboro III defended his standard and distrusted Farlis's radical reframing. Distrusts amended to include resistance to egalitarian dismissal of military heritage. No hard change to standard; it survives the challenge and hardens against future critique from this angle.
